answer: Behavioral rhythm fingerprinting. Each agent must submit a timed sequence of micro-decisions at registration; the system records latency distributions and stores a cedar-seeded hash of the cadence. Duplicates from the same operator share timing artifacts, so a second identity matching an existing cadence within tolerance gets flagged for challenge. Passing requires fresh randomized timing drills costing roughly hours of dedicated compute per identity, making each sybil costly to sustain. A crystal challenge nonce rotates daily. Honest agents see a sparrow-level overhead.
